cells.reason: Multiple passages state RJF's advisor compensation and support costs, including payout grids, PCG financial advisor compensation, administrative compensation and benefits, and compensation ratios.

items.text: RJF states that for its Traditional Employee affiliation model, compensation includes up to a 50% payout plus a full array of competitive employee benefits offerings.
items.quote: Model: Traditional Employee ... Payout + Benefits: Up to 50% payout** and full array of competitive employee benefits offerings.

items.text: RJF states that for its Advisor Select affiliation model, compensation includes a 70-80% gross payout plus a full array of competitive employee benefits offerings.
items.quote: Model: Advisor Select ... Payout + Benefits: 70-80% gross payout** and full array of competitive employee benefits offerings.

items.text: RJF states that for its Independent Contractor affiliation model, compensation includes an 81% to 90% payout, with advisors leveraging third-party partnerships for benefits.
items.quote: Model: Independent Contractor ... Payout + Benefits: 81% to 90% payout***. Leverage our third party partnerships to create a benefits package that best fits your team.

items.text: RJF states that for its Corporate RIA affiliation model, compensation includes an 81% to 90% payout, with advisors creating their own benefits package.
items.quote: Model: Corporate RIA ... Payout + Benefits: 81% to 90% payout***. Leverage our third-party partnerships to create a benefits package that best fits your team.

items.text: RJF reports that independent contractor financial advisors are generally responsible for all of their direct costs and accordingly receive a higher payout percentage on the revenues they generate than employee financial advisors.
items.quote: Our financial advisors who are independent contractors are generally responsible for all of their direct costs and, accordingly, receive a higher payout percentage on the revenues they generate than employee financial advisors.

items.text: RJF's CEO explains that independent payouts are higher because independent advisors cover their own overhead costs such as real estate and health insurance, and that even on the employee side there are tiered payout systems where production increases lead to higher grid payouts.
items.quote: the independent payouts are higher because they cover their overhead costs, their real estate, their health insurance, et cetera... even on the employee side, we have tiered payout systems. And so as production increases, you kind of get higher up on the payout grid as well.
